Magic the Gathering Arena is pretty good way to simulate the Magic the Gathering trading card game. However, this game DOES NOT respect your time. Players are given an absurd amount of time for each of their turns, and are given EXTRA time if they do not take their entire turn time before ending their turn. Players have realized that by taking ALMOST their entire turn timer before passing back, they can frustrate their opponent and hope their opponent misplays or quits out of frustration. And there is NO punishment for this type of "roping". There isn't even a button to report players who are doing this. In addition, the community is more committed to protecting "ropers" than to improve the gameplay experience for all players. Matches that should take 5-10 minutes can take upwards of 45 minutes, for no reason other than WotC and the community allowing it. Imagine playing an action game with 90 second loading screens constantly, that is the experience playing MTGA. When the community ISN'T doing this kind of stuff, the game is pretty dang fun. I continue to play because there are still moments of fun to be found... but I can't in good conscience recommend other people play a game that wastes their time on an unmoving gameboard for minutes at a time.

"If games can be reduced to a simple equation, a possible formula would be (total fun) = (meaningful decisions) / (time played)." - Soren Johnson, Lead Designer of Civilization IV

I like Eternal Card Game better.

On a deeper level, I think Magic suffers as a video game because it will always be tied, at least on some level, to the tabletop cardboard-based game. Eternal (and other digital card games) do not suffer from this limitation and can thus fully explore the features that a fully digital experience offer. Alchemy doesn't count.

The algorithm in this game will determine whether you win or not. You could be the best player in the world, but it will determine if you'll even be able to play minimally or not. It determines which cards you and your opponent will draw based on what's happening in the game, and that will determine the course of the game. NOTHING is even remotely random.

It has a hell queue that counts the points of the cards in your deck (yes, each card has a point value) and will pair you with the worst bad match you'll ever face, if it wants to.

If you want to play a fairer game, play MTGO. I only use that crap game to test IRL decks and because it's free.

Wizards of the Coast's failure to recognize the Arena Team Union and actively pushing against unionizing in a time like now is why I can't in good consciousness recommend Arena to anyone. The game is maintained super well, it's incredible that a complicated set of rules and interactions like Magic the Gathering has is able to be maintained and work seamlessly, and when there is a bug, it gets fixed quickly or prevented from causing issues where it matters. That's the kind of work and devotion the team offers, and when they band together to ask for protections from an increasingly hostile industry, WOTC returns to union busting instead like cowards instead of supporting and trying to actually hear the issues their workers have that enable their best online platform for both learning and playing the game.

Shameless behavior, and absolutely abhorrent. You would be better off going to your local game store, supporting them by asking how to play there or playing at local events. Better yet, refuse to engage with any of WOTC's products until they pull their head out of their asses.
